author: s. g. nava
title: Augusta Medicaid spending for Medicine Services and Procedures reaches $8,090,074 in 2024
text:
Augusta Medicaid providers charged $8,090,074 for Medicine Services and Procedures in 2024, according to data from the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Medicaid Provider Spending database. This figure was up 5.1% compared to 2023, when $7,700,629 in claims were filed in the same category.
Medicaid, a public health program administered by states and funded through both federal and state contributions , provides health coverage for low-income residents, seniors, children and people with disabilities, making it one of the nation’s biggest health care systems.
Since Medicaid is funded by taxpayers, shifts in billing reflect how public health funds are distributed within local communities.
The “Medicine Services and Procedures” category includes a range of Medicaid-billed services, classified by care type using standardized HCPCS and CPT code groupings. For this analysis, each billing code was assigned exclusively to one service category using uniform code prefixes and numbering sequences, enabling more precise tracking of related services and consistent rankings over time.
Though spending increased across several service types, Medicine Services and Procedures ranked fifth by total Medicaid payments in Augusta in 2024.
At the state level, Medicine Services and Procedures ranked sixth for total Medicaid payments in Maine for 2024.
Between 2019 and 2024, Augusta’s Medicaid payments for Medicine Services and Procedures grew by $3,480,662, a rise of 75.5%. Growth was particularly marked in certain periods, with significant year-on-year increases in both 2023 and 2021.
While Medicine Services and Procedures spending was distributed throughout Augusta, it was chiefly concentrated in a few ZIP codes. In 2024, ZIP code 04330 registered $8,049,350 in payments and 04333 reported $40,722. Combined, these 2 ZIP codes made up 100% of Augusta’s payments in this service category that year.
Medicaid payments within the Medicine Services and Procedures category were also concentrated among a small number of billing codes.
Comparing growth, Medicaid payments in Augusta rose by 5.1% for Medicine Services and Procedures from 2023 to 2024, outpacing the 1.7% increase seen for all Medicaid categories citywide during that period.
According to the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services , combined federal and state Medicaid spending totaled about $871.7 billion in fiscal year 2023, representing around 18% of total national health expenditures—an increase from approximately $613.5 billion in 2019 before the COVID-19 pandemic.
This marks nearly 40% growth in just a few years, primarily due to higher enrollment and increased utilization during and after the pandemic.
Federal budget legislation enacted under the Trump administration included sizable measures to reduce federal Medicaid funding and alter how the program operates. The “One Big Beautiful Bill Act,” passed in 2025, is forecast to slash over $1 trillion from federal Medicaid spending over the coming decade and implement policies such as work requirements and greater cost-sharing that could reduce coverage and funding for some recipients. These changes are expected to place greater financial responsibility on states and restrict the growth of federal Medicaid funds, while the program continues to support millions of Americans.
